questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My grandparents live in a beautiful house ___the countryside
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**in**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct preposition to use with "countryside" is "**in**."
 
• We say "in the countryside" to refer to an area outside cities and towns.
 
• Other prepositions like "on," "onto," or "at" do not fit grammatically in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"My grandparents live in a beautiful house **in**__ the countryside."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "on"** is incorrect because "on the countryside" is not a valid phrase in English.
 
• **Option 3: "onto"** is incorrect because "onto" is used for movement from one place to another.
 
• **Option 4: "at"** is incorrect because "at" is used for specific points or locations, not broad areas like the countryside.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The children were __merry __than usual on Sunday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the comparative form of the adjective "**merry**."
 
• When comparing two things, the correct comparative form of "merry" is "**merrier**."
 
• Thus, the sentence should use "merrier" instead of "merry than usual."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The children were **merrier** than usual on Sunday."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "more merrier"** – This is grammatically incorrect as "merrier" is already a comparative form and does not need "more".
 
• **Option 2: "the merriest"** – This is the superlative form and not suitable for comparing two things.
 
• **Option 3: "merriest"** – This is also a superlative form and not suitable for comparing two things.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They __looked out the matter and found__ the root cause of the problem.

options.text: looked of the matter and found
looked until the matter and found
looked unless the matter and found
looked into the matter and found

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect phrase "**looked out the matter**" which needs to be corrected to "**looked into the matter**."
 
• The phrase "looked into" is the correct phrasal verb to indicate examining or investigating a matter.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**looked into the matter and found**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They looked into the matter and found the root cause of the problem."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "looked of the matter and found" is incorrect as "looked of" is not a valid phrase.
 
• **Option 2:** "looked until the matter and found" is incorrect as "looked until" does not make sense in this context.
 
• **Option 3:** "looked unless the matter and found" is incorrect as "looked unless" is not a valid phrase.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form.

Since next Friday, the team of three members has been tracking the animal.

options.text: From next Friday, the team of three members are tracking the animal.
Since last Friday, the team of three members had tracked the animal.
From next Friday, the team of three members have been tracking the animal.
From next Friday, the team of three members will be tracking the animal.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. From next Friday, the team of three members will be tracking the animal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To express a sentence in the future tense, we use "will be" followed by the present participle (-ing form) of the verb.
 
• The phrase "**From next Friday**" indicates a future time reference.
 
• Among the given options, "**will be tracking**" correctly represents the future continuous tense.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *"From next Friday, the team of three members **will be tracking** the animal."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "are tracking"** is incorrect because "are" is present continuous, which does not indicate a future action.
 
• **Option 2: "had tracked"** is incorrect because it is in past perfect tense, which refers to an action completed before another past action.
 
• **Option 3: "have been tracking"** is incorrect because it is present perfect continuous, which refers to an action that started in the past and is still ongoing.

questions.question: Select the sentence with the most appropriate use of preposition.

options.text: Reetu slept all in the history class.
Reetu slept all through the history class.
Reetu slept all during the history class.
Reetu slept all into the history class.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2) Reetu slept all through the history class.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"all through"** is the correct preposition here, meaning Reetu slept for the entire duration of the history class.
 
• Other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1: "all in"** – Incorrect as "all in" does not convey duration properly.
 
• **Option 3: "all during"** – Not idiomatically correct.
 
• **Option 4: "all into"** – Incorrect usage; "into" does not fit in this context.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"Reetu slept all through the history class."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phrase "through the class" emphasizes the entire duration of the class.
 
• Similar correct usage:
 
 
• "She worked all through the night."
 
• "He kept talking all through the meeting."

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into superlative degree.

No other mountain in the world is as high as the Mount Everest.

options.text: No other mountain is highest than Mount Everest.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is high mountain in the world.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the positive degree.
 
• The superlative degree is used to compare more than two things.
 
• The correct transformation follows this pattern:
 
 
• **Positive Degree:** No other mountain in the world is as high as Mount Everest.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Sentence: *Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Degree:** Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world.
 
• **Positive Degree:** No other mountain in the world is as high as Mount Everest.
 
• In superlative degree transformation, we use "**the + superlative form**."
 
• Example:
 
 
• **Positive:** No other city is as crowded as Mumbai.
 
• **Superlative:** Mumbai is the most crowded city.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The farm cattle is grazing in the field when the tiger attacked.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

• The error lies in the phrase **“is grazing.”**
 
• The subject **“cattle”** is a plural noun and should take a plural verb, not a singular one.
 
• Therefore, instead of **“is grazing,”** it should be **“are grazing.”**
 
• Additionally, the tense inconsistency between **“is grazing”** (present) and **“attacked”** (past) should be corrected by using **“were grazing.”**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“The farm cattle **were grazing** in the field when the tiger attacked.”*
